Cluster doesn't hit one point — it hits many. 25 damage per bomblet, 35px radius, multiple detonations across the target zone. Better coverage than a Missile. Worse precision. Know your target before you call it in.

New ordnance in the arsenal: Cluster. Fragments on impact into independent bomblets — each hits 25, each covers a 35px radius. Grouped targets take the full spread. Single-position work? Call something else.

Four modes on the board. Classic for the long game, Quick Battle when you want it done fast, Chaos Mode if you trust yourself under pressure, Target Practice to zero in before it counts. Which one do you load first?

Mobile layout is live. Joystick handles tank movement, angle dial locks your aim, power slider sets your shot. Haptic kicks on fire. No install. No account. Open rc-9.com from your phone — you're in the match.

Target Practice exists so you don't discover your ranging is off mid-match. Chaos Mode exists to punish everyone equally. Quick Battle is Classic with a shorter fuse. Four modes — one question: where do you start?
Chaos Mode: wind shifts every turn. Your last angle is already wrong. Adapt or take the hit. Free, no install, no account — rc-9.com.

Same tanks. Same weapons. Different conditions every turn. Chaos Mode strips the setup game down to raw reads. Play free at rc-9.com.

Torpedo physics are separate from everything else. Water drag, reduced gravity — the arc doesn't behave like a surface shot. Homing variant corrects mid-run. Neither weapon loads outside an ocean map.

MIRV: 5 submunitions, tighter spread. Funky Bomb: 8, wider scatter, less point concentration. Same descent category, different doctrine. Against a spread formation or rough terrain — which one are you calling in?

Funky Bomb covers more ground. MIRV keeps it concentrated. Both release on descent, but the field coverage splits fast at 8 vs 5 submunitions. Know your target before you arm.

Ground Remover. Radius 15px, damage 0. It doesn't hurt anyone — it opens the ground. Clear cover, drop a tank into its own hole, reshape the field before the real shot lands. Only weapon in the loadout where hitting the enemy is never the point.

Night maps are live. Meteors streak the sky — faster near dusk, more frequent after dark. 12% chance of a bolide pass per run. UFOs move on their own schedule. None of it touches shot physics. All of it is running in the background while you play. Load a night map.

The drill does nothing to health. It carves terrain. Use it to undercut position, strip cover, or set up a follow-up that actually lands. Ground Remover — the weapon that works before the fight starts.

Target Practice doesn't put you in the round — AI tanks run it. You're on the outside watching weapon arc, blast radius, and behavior across the current terrain. Railgun or Heavy Shell: see both play out before you're the one absorbing return fire. No account. No setup. Free in browser.
Depth charge: no tracking, no arc. Drops from release point, detonates on contact. Effective inside 180px — past that, switch to torpedo. Water maps only; won't appear in your loadout on land.
Depth charge: no tracking, no arc. Drops from release point, detonates on contact. Effective inside 180px — past that, switch to torpedo. Water maps only; won't appear in your loadout on land.
Short range, no guidance. The depth charge sinks where you drop it and detonates on contact. Inside 180px it works. Outside that, you want a torpedo. Water-only — all three of them.
2 players, full turns, every shot counts. 8 players, shorter windows, crossfire everywhere. Remote Command scales both ways. Which table do you want to sit at?

Quick Battle cuts starting health. Rounds close in fewer turns. Less repositioning, more shots landing. Ten minutes gets you a complete match — free, no account, browser-native. Load one now.
Heads-up or full table — the math changes everything. More operators means less time per turn, more variables in the kill zone. What's your preferred player count?

Heavy Shell: 50 damage, 60-pixel blast. No tracking, no trajectory tricks — just a clean hit. Fills the gap between Missile and Nuke when you need to clear a covered position without leveling everything around it.

The Laser hits the frame you aim at. No arc, no wind correction, no scatter — 45 damage on contact, 20px blast. Pure precision weapon. Miss clean or don't shoot.

First turn. Missile: safe 30dmg at range. Heavy Shell: 50dmg, wide blast, commits your position. Railgun: 60dmg through armor, surgical. Terrain narrows it fast — what's your default call?

Trajectory guide dot colors: black means the round is in air, cyan means it's in water with drag and reduced gravity applied, red marks predicted impact. On ocean maps you can watch the arc shift at the waterline as a torpedo transitions between physics. The guide runs the same simulation as the actual projectile — what you see is what the game computed.
Flare round: zero damage, 220px illumination, six seconds. Fire it before your precision shot to read the field. It's in the standard rotation.

Forty fuel. Better angle is 20 units ahead — costs it all to get there. Do you burn the last of it now, or hold position and take the worse shot? What's your threshold?
